messages:
Maya (Support): Hey team — greenbilling just escalated, seeing ~15-20% 429s for their /v1/generate route starting 2026-04-14 11:38 PDT. Their volume was steady but they had a short spike due to a retry loop in their worker pool. Customer says SDK v0.9.3, 8 concurrent workers

John R (SRE): Can you paste one of the failing request-ids and the response headers? Preferably the X-RateLimit-* headers and Retry-After if present. Also which region were they hitting?

Maya (Support): One example request-id: req_20260414_938_A1. Hitting us-west-2. Attached snippet from their logs (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000/min
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 28
Retry-After: 6
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "rate limit exceeded" }
```

Ashwin (Eng): That header set looks like they're hitting an RPM window. Limit looks high but Remaining==0 and Reset short -> token-bucket exhausted. Do we have telemetry showing per-key burst credits? Maya, can you pull their per-key rpm/tpm curve in the console for the 10m window around the spike?

Maya (Support): Console graph attached (screenshot). Spike from 11:37-11:39 up to 9k rpm for ~90s then drop. Also customer sent their client backoff code — they had immediate fixed-interval retries with no jitter (0.5s) and 8 concurrent workers, so they amplified the burst.

Lina (SRE): That's classic retry amplification. Two parallel things to do: 1) advise customer to add exponential backoff + full jitter and cap concurrency; 2) short-term, we can grant a temporary burst window or raise their per-key burst limit for 24h while they deploy the fix.

John R (SRE): Agreed. Also check if the gateway queueing/burst smoothing layer dropped requests before hitting downstream. Run: `redwoodctl metrics query "sum(rate(api_request_total{customer=\"greenbilling\",code=\"429\"}[1m])) by (route)` and paste results.

Ashwin (Eng): For repro steps we recommend a small bench with `hey` or `wrk` replicating their concurrency and retry pattern. Example command to reproduce approximate behavior: 
```
# single-process, concurrent 8 clients, 1s rate
hey -z 90s -c 8 -q 0 -m POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" -d '{"prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```
Capture response headers to confirm Retry-After.

Maya (Support): Ran the metrics query per request from John, snippet: `route=/v1/generate -> 18 429s/min at peak`. Also saw small bump in error budget token events.

John R (SRE): Ok. Action plan: (A) Offer customer a temporary +30% burst allowance for 6 hours and enable per-route smoothing for /v1/generate in us-west-2; (B) Ask them to deploy a client fix (exp backoff + jitter + cap concurrency to 4) — provide code sample; (C) schedule an SRE follow-up to watch the key.

Ashwin (Eng): I'll prepare a short sample patch for their SDK:
```
// pseudo JS retry with full jitter
async function retry(fn, attempts=5) {
  for (let i=0;i<attempts;i++){
    try { return await fn(); }
    catch(e){
      const backoff = Math.random() * Math.min(1000 * Math.pow(2,i), 5000);
      await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, backoff));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('max retries');
}
```
Recommend max concurrency 4 and max retries 3.

Maya (Support): Customer accepted patch plan; asked if we can do immediate mitigation while they roll.

Lina (SRE): I can provision a temporary policy. Creating Jira to track: INF-4587 (temporary burst bump + smoothing). I'll add owners and rollback conditions.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: policy/rlimit-adjustment for customer=greenbilling, change_id=chg-9874, starts=2026-04-14T19:05:00Z

Maya (Support): Thanks Lina. Also logged a support ticket with the customer (TICKET-8932) with recommended client changes and repro steps. Sent the sample SDK patch.

John R (SRE): After change goes live we'll watch these metrics for one full hour. If 429s persist with Retry-After present and Remaining==0, escalate to eng-runtime to check token bucket refills and cross-customer interference.

Maya (Support): Customer confirms they're testing an SDK change on staging now. Will push patch to prod in ~45m.

Ashwin (Eng): Notes for eng-runtime if escalated: check kernel selection for the routing agent and the per-worker queue length. Also inspect KV cache hit/miss — if prefix-cache misses coincide with spike we may see per-request cost increase and thus effective capacity drop.

Lina (SRE): Monitoring checklist I used: 1) per-key 1m/5m rpm & tpm; 2) X-RateLimit header series for sample requests; 3) gateway queue length; 4) downstream model latency P95; 5) token-bucket refill logs. I set alerts on >5% of customer requests returning 429 in a 2m window.

Maya (Support): Update: customer rolled to prod at 12:28 PDT with the jitter/backoff patch + concurrency cap. Early signs: 429s dropped to baseline (<0.5%). They reported small success.

John R (SRE): Great. Lina, please close INF-4587 when the temporary policy is revoked and confirm the rollback. Also add a note recommending they consider Dedicated capacity if they need consistent high concurrency.

Lina (SRE): Will do. revocation scheduled in 24h unless customer asks to extend. INF-4587 updated with post-mortem checklist.

Maya (Support): Customer grateful. Sent post-mortem email with reproduce commands, SDK snippet, and suggested rate-limit-aware patterns (batching, caching). Closing loop. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reminder: please add a short postmortem to #postmortems within 72h per process.

Maya (Support): Will file a short postmortem and link INF-4587 + TICKET-8932. Thanks everyone.

John R (SRE): Thanks — feel free to ping if anything resurfaces.

Lina (SRE): Closing our watch. :white_check_mark:
